chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from a man, from Mandal ibn Ali al-'Abri, from Muhammad ibn Matraf, from Misma', from al-Asbagh ibn Nabatah, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah, Exalted and Mighty, becomes angry with a city but does not send down punishment upon it, its prices rise, its lifespans shorten, its merchants do not profit, its fruits do not fall, its rivers do not flow, its rains are withheld, and its wicked people are given power over it.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of Allah's anger upon a city before punishment arrives?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this chain to illustrate the concept of 'tadhalluf' (humiliation) as a precursor to direct chastisement, a theme central to Shia eschatological reflections on societal decay. The narration links material instability—such as inflated prices and barren lands—with moral corruption, suggesting that economic distress serves as a divine warning to the community before the imposition of severe punishment.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Abbas b. Ma’ruf from a man from Mandal b. Ali al-’Abri from Muhammad b. Matraf from Masma’ from al-Asbagh b. Nabateh from Ali (a.s.) who said: “

If Allah gets angry over a city but does not reveal His chastisement upon it, it faces inflation, lifespan of people is reduced, trade becomes profitless, there is shortage of fruits, rivers become dry, rainfall becomes scanty and mischief-mongers are made to overpower them.”
